content.title: Marshawn Lynch Joins Euphoria Season 3 as Series Honors Late Actors
content.text: Published Apr 20, 2026 - 09:22 Last Update Apr 20, 2026 - 09:22 © Marshawn Lynch jokes he's 'not old enough' to watch his Euphoria roleTV Dramas Smallest Font Largest Font Former NFL running back Marshawn Lynch joined the cast of the HBO drama Euphoria for its Season 3 premiere on April 12, 2026, marking a significant career shift for the Super Bowl champion. The premiere also featured emotional tributes to late cast members Eric Dane and Angus Cloud as the series returned under creator Sam Levinson.Lynch, who played 12 seasons for the Seattle Seahawks, admitted to being startled by the show's intense and mature themes during his preparation. The 39-year-old actor previously appeared in the 2023 film Bottoms before being personally recruited by Levinson for the Emmy-winning series. According to Art Threat, Lynch expressed a deep commitment to being viewed as a serious dramatic actor alongside co-star Zendaya. "Let’s just say I had fun in that motherf–ker. I was trying to hold my own and trying not to be the motherf–cker that they’re waiting on to get your sh-t together." said Lynch, the former NFL star.Movies The production also navigated the loss of two prominent actors prior to the season's release. Eric Dane, known for his role as Cal Jacobs, passed away at age 53 following a battle with ALS. Director Sam Levinson coordinated with Dane to film his final scenes in a single day to accommodate his declining health before his death, as reported by E! Online. "Eric called me before we started shooting and told me that he had been diagnosed with ALS," said Levinson, the series creator.Levinson detailed how the production adjusted the set environment to support Dane during his final performance as the father of Nate Jacobs. "We had a lot of conversations about just life and what that meant. I loved him very deeply, and I said, ‘Eric, whatever shape you show up in, we’re gonna make it work. I have faith that it’s all gonna work.’" Levinson continued.The showrunner noted that Dane's character remained a vital part of the narrative despite the actor's physical challenges."He showed up and I could tell he had a slight slur in his voice and he told me that," stated Levinson. To explain the change in the actor's speech, the production utilized environmental cues within the scene."I said, ‘Don’t worry. We’ll just put, like, five beer bottles in front of you and you’ve been drinking all night.’ He was like, ‘Perfect, perfect.’ And his character, it was such a gift." Levinson added.The premiere also addressed the absence of Angus Cloud, who died in 2023 at age 25. Rather than writing the character off through death, Levinson chose to keep Cloud's character, Fezco, alive within the show's universe, sentencing him to 30 years in prison. This decision was a personal tribute to the actor's real-life struggles. "I fought very hard to keep him clean when he was alive, and losing him was really tough," remarked Levinson.The creator reflected on the emotional impact of the loss and his desire to provide a different ending for the character than what occurred in reality."I felt like if I couldn’t keep him alive in life, then, I could in the show." said Levinson. In a formal statement provided to Entertainment Weekly, Levinson elaborated on how the epidemic of fentanyl overdoses influenced the tone of the final season.Arts & Entertainment"With addiction, you're supposed to be prepared for the loss of someone struggling, but his death stirred an anger—not only for him, but for the many young lives in America cut short by fentanyl," wrote Levinson.The showrunner concluded that the season serves as a memorial for those who did not receive second chances in their battles with addiction. "This season became my way to honor Angus and all the kids who weren’t offered a second chance. I wanted to tell a story where hope and light could still be felt in the darkness." Levinson stated.DetailInformationCo-StarZendaya, Sydney Sweeney, Jacob ElordiAnnouncement DateFebruary 14, 2025Series CreatorSam LevinsonNetworkHBO (Max streaming)The season premiere included a title card in remembrance of Eric Dane and a secondary memorial screen for Angus Cloud and executive producer Kevin Turen.
